holderPosition.says: The holder owns a Securitize share of the same class as the NYSE stock, with one vote per share and any dividend, and no SPV or receipt in between. Whether the holder stays the holder of record in their own name on Continental's book after conversion, or a Securitize entity takes that line with the token ledger as a sub-register, is not published; holding requires onboarding by Securitize's broker-dealer and a whitelisted wallet.

outside.says: Inbound: move shares out of street name by DRS or DWAC to Continental, which registers the holder, then convert to tokens in a Securitize-registered wallet. Outbound: no published procedure, burn address, time or fee.

Securitize decides the authoritative chain on a fork, may migrate assets to another fork, and keeps manual safeguards over ownership records as transfer agent. On chain one key can claw back, pause or change the split multiplier.
One vote per share and any dividend (none expected); no process for voting from a token wallet is published.

Delaware corporate law for the share and register; federal securities law for the listing, the transfer agents and the broker-dealer. NYSE is the reference market; on-chain trading is thin and the switch latency is unpublished.

verdict.summary: An origin of kind share with transfer-agent register entries says what the holder has, and the issuer's own terms are filed under Securities Act liability. But which record governs (Continental's register or Securitize's control book, and Securitize choosing the chain on a fork) needs the authoritative-record proposal, no transfer agent publishes any entry, cross-chain totals have no structure, and every signer except Continental and the SEC is one group, which v3 cannot show.
